title: extcap: Add ability to enable SHA-1 algorithms
description:
libssh 0.10.0 removed SHA-1 based keys and algorithms from its
default configuration, though they are still supported. We
ship with 0.10.5 in Windows and macOS now, and many Linux
distributions are on 0.10.x as well.

Add the ability to re-enable SHA-1 RSA keys, MAC, and KEX algorithms
with a preference to ciscodump, sshdump, and wifidump.

This will be a little easier in 0.11.0, where it's possible to
just specify the algorithms you want to add to the default list,
instead of having to specify the entire list.

Fix #19510. Fix #19594

notes.body: May be wait libssh 0.11.0 ? there is an ETA about this new release ?

They haven't announced anything yet, but I would guess it would be soon.

For the meantime, people can use Wireshark 4.0.x if they have an affected device (some of which are Cisco routers that can't be updated.)

Maybe defer for a little bit, but if we get close to 4.4.0 and libssh 0.11.0 isn't out yet, push it so that there's a supported version that works once Wireshark 4.0.x is out of support?

Ah, here's an ETA on libssh 0.11.0: https://gitlab.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/-/milestones

June 30, 2024. So it's maybe ok to wait?

You could probably wait, for the distributions we control (Windows, Mac). However, there are other platforms which may/will not have that new version available. So getting this out for both versions makes sense.

Yes, for example, I wouldn't expect RHEL 9 to necessarily update to 0.11.0 when it's released.
I assume that the motivation for the new configuration syntax to add back the algorithms was precisely people needing to add back SHA-1 algorithms. Too bad it didn't make it in at the same time as they removed them.

SSH_OPTIONS_PUBLICKEY_ACCEPTED_TYPES was introduced in libssh 0.8.3. According to our lib requirement, we still support libssh 0.6.0 (My build error was on 0.7.1 (RHEL7.9))

I have no problem if we would higher the lib requirement to ex 0.9.3 which is Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, or 0.9.6 (Ubuntu 22.04/RHEL8)

or turn off this option, which seems to build, #if LIBSSH_VERSION_INT \>= SSH_VERSION_INT(0,8,3)
Better turn off the whole block, see !14078
